title.narrative: Constituents improve capacity to ensure adequate and effective labour protection and rights at work for all

description.narrative:
a) Minimum wages According to the Global Wage Report 2020/21 approximately 134 million workers in the Asia-Pacific region receive wages below the minimum wage threshold. Inflation rates are eroding the purchasing power of minimum wages worldwide, affecting 160 million workers in the region that are paid at and below the minimum wage (ILO, 2021). This situation raises concerns about the ability of the workers and their families to cope with the cost-of living crisis, putting them at risk of poverty and deprivation. Setting adequate minimum wages and their periodic revision is essential in protecting workers from unduly low pay and even preventing workers from falling into poverty and ensuring that their wage maintains its purchasing capacity, compensating for the erosion from inflation. ILO’s assistance to countries includes policy briefs on wage setting practices in different countries, knowledge sharing of the different minimum wage systems, raising awareness on living wage, and research on living wage trends and developments in the region.
b) Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Asia and the Pacific region is seriously hit by fatal occupational injuries and its impact on people's life and business are huge. However, reporting on fatal occupational injuries raise challenges. ILO’s assistance in this area includes the development of a system of recording and notification of occupational accidents and diseases including improved coordination mechanism among ministries and institutions which are engaged in the registry of occupational accidents and diseases, development of country-specific tools on recording and notification of occupational accidents and diseases , building capacity of labour inspectors and other concerned officials in the collection of data and investigation of occupational accidents, raising awareness and improving the capacity of employers and workers in the reporting, recording and notification of occupational accidents and diseases, resear
